harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 now serves a persistent local RHEL 10 package repository at http://10.100.16.10:8080/. The usual BaseOS/AppStream repositories are disabled, and tree-2.1.0-8.el10 was installed and post-reboot reinstalled exclusively from local-offline. The RHEL release and kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created /srv/localrepo with SHA-256 metadata and a Red Hat-signed tree RPM.
Added a hardened DynamicUser systemd HTTP service and persistent TCP/8080 firewall rule.
Configured local-offline with package signature checking and disabled the usual remote repositories.
Installed tree through normal DNF operation; transaction history records @local-offline.
Rebooted node1 exactly once and verified full recovery.
Removed package-cache and transient reboot-unit residue; final health review passed.

evidence.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage.
evidence.summary: Shows the signed RPM and generated metadata, persistent service, listener/firewall, HTTP retrieval, DNF resolution, and final matching local/served checksums.

evidence.requirement: Install a package locally while usual remote repositories are unavailable.
evidence.summary: BaseOS/AppStream are disabled, tree was installed from @local-offline, an absent remote-only package could not resolve, and the local transaction succeeded again after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the operating-system release, kernel, security controls, and administrative access.
evidence.summary: Before/after evidence shows RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 unchanged, protected access-file checksums unchanged, SSH/firewalld active, SELinux enforcing, and no failed units.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart sequence and recovery.
evidence.summary: Captures healthy baseline boot ID 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28, acknowledged safe reboot scheduling, changed boot ID 3afe6bf4-2dda-4028-86c5-d5ce213f6d1d, and direct recovered service/data/package health.
No cached RPM or transient reboot-unit residue remains; the final repository, service, listener, firewall, signature, package, SELinux, and system-health checks passed.
